about: The answers candidate's cast and trigger rules with the attack left to Forge (no attack policy), for a side-by-side run on the same tables. Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Version 2 = the crew candidate (version 1: its attack block, triggers and every cast rule) with answer rules in front and the cards the engine rules starved given a place. Written from the 200 tables of ab-run #27 (seed 20261260, pool bots-v2, opponents under their playbooks), where the candidate won 52 and the stock pilot 36. Rules 1-2, the symmetric wipes Blood Money and Blasphemous Act: (1) an opponent could kill us next turn with more power than we have (threat >= life, opp_power > power); (2) an opponent has five creatures and ten power or more, more power than our whole board. Under version 1 they were cast in 3 of 48 and 11 of 44 games drawn and were in hand at 23 and 16 losses (stock: 27 of 42, 25 of 38): rule 4's list always had something to cast, so Forge never got to them. The deck rebuilds after a wipe: Brass comes back from the command zone and returns a dead Pirate each combat, Blood Money pays Treasures for our nontoken creatures. Forge may still cast them when the rules are idle, as before. Rules 3-4, Evacuation: held, released only when threat >= life, and played by rule 3 after combat (main2) when an opponent could kill us and has more power. Under both pilots Forge cast it in our own main phase, mostly at 30 to 40 life against two to five creatures, bouncing our own board: the seat won 2 of the 34 games in which it was cast under each pilot (4 of 68). Rules 5-8 are version 1's rules 1-3 and the first seven cards of its rule 4 (the lords and engines), unchanged. Rule 9: Hostage Taker and Feed the Swarm when an opponent has a creature (Feed the Swarm is aimed by Forge and cast only when Forge's logic agrees). Rule 10: Coercive Recruiter when an opponent has a creature (each Pirate that enters later steals a creature until end of turn). Rule 11: the rest of version 1's rule 4 up to Breeches, unchanged. Rule 12: Dire Fleet Ravager while our board has at least the power of the strongest opponent (a third of everyone's life helps the player ahead on board). Rule 13: Distant Melody (version 1's rule 7, moved up from behind the creature list and lowered from four Pirates to three). Rule 14: the rest of version 1's rule 4 with Merchant Raiders and Amphin Mutineer at its head, The Grim Captain's Locker moved up behind The Indomitable, Captivating Crew behind Azure Fleet Admiral, Dire Fleet Daredevil added among the two-drops. Rule 16: Captivating Crew's steal before combat when an opponent has a creature (Forge picks the target). Rule 22: Rakdos Charm (AI:RemoveDeck:All, never cast by either pilot, in hand at 30 losses) after combat; Forge chooses the mode and target. Local check, 16 tables of bots (seeds 20263140, 20263141): Hostage Taker cast in 6 of 6 games drawn (took Vincent, Emmara), Coercive Recruiter 3 of 4 (stole commanders: Caesar, Emmara), Captivating Crew's steal used, Rakdos Charm cast twice (graveyard mode), Evacuation cast twice at 6 life and against a 24-creature board, Blood Money twice (once 2 of our creatures against 7). The attack is version 1's, untouched.
